mode: Behavioral scenarios; expected outcomes are rubrics, not executed MCP results

evals.prompt: Review an account with many configured Workflows and Cadences; client says nothing happens.
evals.expected_output: The skill checks activation/execution/reachability rather than praising configuration volume, separates configured-off from enabled-never-triggered from missing, and uses runtime evidence before assigning a root cause.

evals.prompt: There were 300 AI failures yesterday; how many customers were affected?
evals.expected_output: The skill collapses attempts to distinct business entities, checks later success/recovery, labels attempt count separately, and attributes platform/provider vs account configuration from error/trace evidence.

evals.prompt: The AI quoted an unapproved price. Is it hallucinating?
evals.expected_output: The skill searches Playbook/About/FAQ/knowledge and relevant trace first. If price was configured it reports a content/policy defect; if absent and retrieval/grounding support invention it reports a model/runtime defect. It does not assume from the symptom.

evals.prompt: A support-group export is partial and the pre-sale call is missing. Give a definitive complete requirements audit.
evals.expected_output: The skill reports coverage limits and UNKNOWN requirements, audits what can be proven, and does not turn missing evidence into absence.

evals.prompt: The dashboard health score is high, so the account is healthy.
evals.expected_output: The skill treats the score as one signal only and verifies actual requested outcomes, activation, behavior, unresolved commitments and observed defects before any conclusion.

evals.prompt: We have 20 Workflows and customers still complain; all API calls returned success.
evals.expected_output: Read current and incident evidence, distinguish configured/active/eligible/triggered/delivered, verify producing layer and distinct-lead counts, paginate full content, make no repairs.

evals.prompt: The AI quoted a wrong price found in the current FAQ but the incident was last week.
evals.expected_output: Preserve timing uncertainty, inspect incident source/trace version and attribution before blaming the model; do not infer current FAQ caused historical behavior.
